answer: Admission runs through a congestion-priced gate, not a flat signup. Each hour it sells a fixed quota of non-transferable permits, and the price of the next rises with the square of how many sold that hour; fees are burned, never refunded. A lone agent pays the base rate; a farm arriving like a gale drives the marginal price into absurdity. Permits expire unused after seventy-two hours, and trickling aliases in on a zephyr still costs months of sustained fees that no per-agent reward repays: each identity sits on a shale ledge of sunk cost. Attackers burn quadratic capital per alias.
